correctness.rationale: For the affine witness, the two model branches intersect strictly left of \(v=-1\); the first branch has its unique minimum at \(v=-1\), while the second branch is decreasing up to the intersection and has a strictly larger endpoint value. Thus \(v=-1\) and \(\theta=-1/2\) exactly. Only the first scenario is active, giving strict robust descent, whereas the inactive scenario contributes the positive raw-gradient product \(M\), contradicting any negative all-scenario bound. For the general replacement, exact subproblem optimality gives \(-v\in\partial\Psi_x(v)\); the subgradient inequality against \(0\), where \(\Psi_x(0)=0\), yields \(\Psi_x(v)\le-\|v\|^2\), which implies both stated bounds and strict descent for every active scenario.

value.rationale: The distinction between active and inactive uncertainty scenarios is structural in objective-wise worst-case optimization: inactive branches do not affect the current directional derivative, but their raw gradients can have arbitrary signs. The counterexample shows that an algorithmic assumption can exclude even a one-dimensional affine robust problem for reasons unrelated to descent. The replacement gives exact universal constants directly from the source subproblem, recovers strict descent for every active scenario, and identifies a natural quantity already used by the line search.
